title: ASEAN Plus Three: Marcos calls for urgent action amid economic pressures
summary: President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. on Tuesday underscored the urgent need for the ASEAN member-states, as well as China, Japan, and Republic of Korea to put their collective strength to work…

blocks.text: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., China Minister of Agriculture and Rural Affairs Zhang Zhu, and Singaporean Prime Minister Lawrence Wong prepare to pose for a group picture during the 29th ASEAN Plus Three Summit, part of the 49th ASEAN Summit, on November 17, 2026 in Manila, Philippines. Ezra Acayan/Pool via REUTERS

President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. on Tuesday underscored the urgent need for the ASEAN member-states, as well as China, Japan, and Republic of Korea to put their collective strength to work to respond to current global economic challenges.

Marcos made the call during the 29th ASEAN Plus Three (APT) Summit, which was also attended by Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae, South Korean President Lee Jae Myung, and Chinese Agriculture Minister Zhang Zhu.

“A disruption thousands of miles away can reach households across East and Southeast Asia through the price of rice, the cost of energy, or the loss of a day's income. Our peoples feel the effects of the global economy in palpable and immediate ways,” Marcos said.
“The benefits of regional cooperation, in turn, should be just as tangible and reach our peoples with the same urgency,” he added.
Marcos also noted that APT has served as one of East Asia's most important platforms for stability, resilience, and shared prosperity for nearly three decades now.
He said that this regional cooperation connects the markets, industries, technology, and investment of ASEAN member-states with China, Japan, and the Republic of Korea.
“Acting together, we can give our peoples greater security today and greater confidence for tomorrow,” Marcos said.
“With ASEAN at its center, the partnership gives us a platform to act on our common stake in a stable, connected region that sustains growth and opportunity for all,” he added.

ASEAN leaders are set to adopt on Tuesday two ASEAN Plus Three Leaders’ statements---one on maritime trade and logistics connectivity, and another on strengthening energy and food security resilience amid external shocks and supply chain disruptions. — RSJ, GMA News
